study_info.title: Intensive insulin therapy prevents the progression of diabetic microvascular complications in Japanese patients with non-insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus: a randomized prospective 6-year study
study_info.authors: Yasuo Ohkubo, Hideki Kishikawa, Eiichi Araki, Takao Miyata, Satoshi Isami, Sadatoshi Motoyoshi, Yujiro Kojima, Naohiko Furuyoshi, Motoaki Shichiri
study_info.study_design: Randomized prospective clinical trial; randomization method not detailed
study_info.inclusion_criteria: NIDDM patients treated with 1 or 2 daily injections of intermediate-acting insulin, no retinopathy or simple retinopathy determined by clinical funduscopic evaluation, urinary albumin excretion < 300 mg/24 h and serum creatinine level < 1.5 mg/dl, absence of diabetic somatic or autonomic neuropathy severe enough to require treatment, < 70 years of age, and otherwise healthy (no other findings such as hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, severe diabetic complications or other severe medical conditions), diagnosed as NIDDM by no history of ketoacidosis, negative islet cell antibody, and daily urinary C-peptide excretion more than 20 μg.
study_info.exclusion_criteria: Diabetic somatic or autonomic neuropathy severe enough to require treatment, age 70 years or older, hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, severe diabetic complications or other severe medical conditions, history of ketoacidosis, positive islet cell antibody, daily urinary C-peptide excretion 20 μg or less.
study_info.study_setting: Out-patient clinic at Kumamoto University School of Medicine
study_info.source_of_recruitment: Patients from the out-patient clinic at Kumamoto University School of Medicine
study_info.dropout_reasons: Death (3 patients), moved to another city (3 patients), changed therapy group (2 patients)

minimal_units.intervention_details: Insulin 3 or more times daily (rapid-acting insulin at each meal and intermediate-acting insulin at bedtime). Dosage adjusted according to self-monitored blood glucose.
